[head=2][color=#535961]Shinohara Heavy Industries[/color][/head]
Shinohara is Crescent's largest corporate power. Its doctrine is continuity through infrastructure: governments change, but compatible parts, debt schedules, freight networks, clone records, and drydocks can keep producing revenue.
[head=3][color=#535961]Executive[/color][/head]
- [bold]Sector Manager.[/bold] Answers to the wider company for return, asset security, and future market position. - [bold]Board Executive.[/bold] Converts corporate goals into contracts, quotas, and branch policy. - [bold]Human Resources Officer.[/bold] Handles personnel, discipline, housing, benefits, and the dependency built into employment.
[head=3][color=#535961]Security and staff[/color][/head]
- [bold]Head of CorpSec.[/bold] Directs protection of personnel, contracts, patents, and physical assets. - [bold]CorpSec Agent.[/bold] Prevents loss and keeps ordinary business operating. - [bold]Corporate Liquidation Agent.[/bold] Ends high-risk situations after prevention has failed. - [bold]Salaryman[/bold] and [bold]MedTech Researcher.[/bold] Keep the integrated commercial, medical, technical, and research system running.
Shinohara violence is judged by economic outcome. Protecting an asset without destroying its customers is better than winning an expensive battle for prestige.
[head=3][color=#535961]How to address them[/color][/head]
Use polished corporate manners. Address superiors by office, such as Manager or Director; [color=#535961][bold]Sir[/bold][/color] or [color=#535961][bold]Ma'am[/bold][/color] is safe. Rank in the company is rank in the room.
